# API child failure PostgreSQL evidence

Task #2234 depends on APP guard #2231, process harness #2233 and independent evidence validator #2236. Existing #2183 remains blocked until final composition review and exact-head ordinary/race/required CI pass. Existing full API 252/27/9 gate is unchanged and mandatory; it does not cover the explicit bootstrap diagnostic here.

The new matrix pins official Go 1.23.12 and creates only its own postgres:17 container on a loopback-only ephemeral port. A keeper shell is PID1 and runs the unchanged official entrypoint/postgres child with ordinary test authentication. Each mode compiles the actual test executable. Separate databases identify focused green, original success, missing-ownership bootstrap, and guard-removal red runs. Bootstrap requires guard barrier/release, exact exit1 and actual reap, then observes zero connections before service disposal. It never guesses a schema name.

The red source is an uncommitted archive copy with only the actual child dispatch changed from guarded wrapper to direct child call. Its original:fatal harness must fail at the inherited cleanup assertion, preserve a live original immutable backend at the cleanup barrier, and show a different server session attempting the exact owned DROP. Neither red source nor its binary is a mergeable change.

JSON collector settings are verified, rotation/truncation disabled, positive SELECT/CREATE/DROP controls bracket execution, and the entire directory is archived after graceful owned-service shutdown, then extracted and checked against the archive and hash inventory. Missing files, markers, malformed/truncated JSON, unclean shutdown, or unexpected DROP statements fail verification. Same-session sequence numbers bind permitted parent DROP to the observer's reaped-backends-absent marker; timestamps alone are not an ordering proof. The observer's exact PID/backend_start is carried in both independent observations and SQL markers.

Artifacts retain source/tree, binary hashes, red patch, raw Go JSON, bootstrap raw output, effective logging settings, container shutdown state, complete collector files and their hashes. Expected child failures are diagnostic witnesses, not skipped or successful ordinary acceptance cases. Unexpected output, timeouts, log ambiguity or inability to reproduce red must be investigated, never manually rerun as a substitute for diagnosis.

No production configuration, shared fixtures, existing workflows, authentication or repository permissions are changed. The dedicated #2236 adversarial controls run before integration; their synthetic results do not claim Go/PG execution. This CI candidate still requires independent review and real exact-head execution.

Postmaster exit is not collector flush. Before stopping PostgreSQL, the controller records the actual postmaster and logger PID/start-tick identities as OS postgres, requiring unmasked live start_code/end_code ranges and verifies their parent relationship inside this container. It uses pg_ctl fast stop as OS postgres, observes that exact logger gone, and checks keeper reaped postmaster exit0. DEBUG1 logging provides the logger's explicit pipe-EOF/flush marker. Only then is the complete log archive captured and hashed; keeper is released afterward. Collector metadata links container identity, process snapshots, ordered monotonic boundaries and archive bytes. No backend PID is signaled.

The verifier must validate collector metadata and the actual logger EOF marker in addition to all known schema-admin/session boundaries. Archive/hash agreement alone establishes copy integrity, not absence of omitted server activity. Failure cleanup disposes only this newly created container and never marks an incomplete drain as accepted. Docker exit0 alone is insufficient.

Initialization is isolated from evidence logging. Before any entrypoint invocation, the keeper requires empty owned PGDATA/hooks and no evidence directory; the host verifies the actual entrypoint blob8d507bc40798732dc89a1849ce5d80c451af4a1f and records image identity. Phase1 uses collector=off and a socket-only listener. Matching launch PID/start ticks, comm=postgres, PGDATA pidfile and explicit socket readiness distinguish final exec from its temporary server. Effective collector=off is checked. Owner-run pg_ctl fast stop, bounded actual child wait0, no remaining process, existing PG_VERSION and absent evidence directory precede phase2. Initialization output and boundary metadata are retained. Phase2 uses the same image, volume, authentication and official entrypoint, which skips initialization.

Final logging pins C message locale, default verbosity and PROCESS_FALLBACK %p %c prefix. The parser requires precisely the logger EOF diagnostic in both JSON and fallback, never arbitrary fallback. Disconnect callbacks may follow SQL absence; reviewed actual-child reap/immutable absence queries and same-observer marker ordering establish the safe parent DROP gate. Read-only official Go1.23.12 gofmt checks explicitly cover the new guard fixture, corrected original child process test and new failure PG harness, without replacing existing format/full-package gates.

Failure cleanup preserves separately marked best-effort collector archives and process/container/drain diagnostics before disposal; it preserves the original failed status and never treats partial capture as accepted. Keeper reap publication is awaited with a bound. Logger completion requires exact EOF plus observed disappearance, not a zombie exit-code claim; transient zombies are polled, persistent zombies fail. No capability or security setting is expanded, and actual Bash/image identity is retained.
